title: Database per Service

validation.research: Six primary sources: Chris Richardson’s Database per Service catalog, Microsoft’s microservice data considerations, and PostgreSQL Schemas, Privileges, GRANT, and SET ROLE documentation. The established name and hyphenated punctuation alias are preserved. The article distinguishes private ownership from mandatory physical server isolation, private-table/private-schema/server variants, authoritative facts from consumer-owned projections, owner/runtime privileges, and local transactions from explicit cross-service coordination. It does not repeat an overbroad claim that CAP universally prohibits distributed transactions. PGlite’s official documentation was separately consulted for isolated verification, not as the source for the architectural pattern.

runnable_example.engine: PostgreSQL 18.6 (PGlite 0.5.13) on wasm32-unknown-emscripten, compiled by emcc (Emscripten gcc/clang-like replacement + linker emulating GNU ld) 6.0.5 (1db513782be24469589d7cb8a1f1834e9a33f271), 32-bit
runnable_example.verification: Executed both actual SQL fences in a fresh embedded PostgreSQL engine; exact stated result sets and partial progress; transaction-local role reset; owner/runtime roles and flags; own-schema and column grants; no owner membership or public DDL; live cross-service read/write/join denials; runtime DDL/ownership/identity-column denials; successful own-store operations; quantity and uniqueness constraints with unchanged earlier commits; insufficient-stock guard; no cross-service foreign key; owner-only schema evolution and no implicit grants on future objects. PGlite is single connection: no authentication, network, multiserver/concurrency, or production service workflow is tested.

example_limits: Original executable PostgreSQL SQL example of private Orders and Inventory schemas on one shared database. Four NOLOGIN owner/runtime roles are provisioned in a fresh isolated cluster; public CREATE is revoked, new private schemas have no PUBLIC access, runtime roles get only own-store USAGE/SELECT plus Orders INSERT or Inventory UPDATE(available_units). The provisioning administrator uses SET ROLE/SET LOCAL ROLE for permission checks; production separate authentication is not modeled. Inventory starts with five physical units and commits a two-unit local adjustment. A deliberate zero-unit Orders insert raises check_violation, leaving no order while Inventory remains at three. Two live cross-service SQL attempts must raise insufficient_privilege. Exception blocks catch only the expected SQLSTATE class and fail on unexpected success. No API, network, reservation lifecycle, retries, reconciliation, authentication setup, distributed transaction, or production checkout workflow. The host has PostgreSQL clients but no server, so the SQL is verified in an isolated ignored PGlite 0.5.13 runtime using its PostgreSQL 18.6 engine, without project dependency changes. PGlite is single-connection verification and is not a concurrency or production deployment test.

verification_runtime.reason: Native PostgreSQL client programs are installed but the server binary is absent and Docker is not running. An isolated embedded PostgreSQL engine executes the actual SQL without modifying project dependencies or a user database.
verification_runtime.limits: Single-connection permissions and transaction verification only. No production login configuration, network, concurrent connections, multiserver deployment, or service workflow test.

publication: Local implementation only. No publishing, deployment, commit, push, or pull request.
